title: Soft Body Collision Forge
description: A damaged helmet rests on a pedestal while a ShaderBall behaves as a soft, jelly-like projectile the user can launch at it. On impact, the ShaderBall deforms elastically using vertex displacement, wraps partially around the helmet, then slowly recovers its shape. Users control launch angle, velocity, and softness stiffness to experiment with different deformation results.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads DamagedHelmet.glb centered at the origin on a small circular platform and ShaderBall.glb positioned 6 units to the right as a launchable soft body projectile. Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0,3,10) with OrbitControls. Lighting: one DirectionalLight from upper-left, one HemisphereLight for ambient fill, and an optional subtle EnvironmentMap for reflections. Interaction steps: (1) A GUI panel (lil-gui) exposes launch angle (-45 to 45 degrees, default 0), launch velocity (2-20 m/s, default 10), and stiffness (0.01-1.0, default 0.3). (2) User clicks a 'Launch' button in the GUI to fire the ShaderBall toward the helmet. (3) Animate the ShaderBall along a parabolic arc toward the helmet. (4) On proximity detection (bounding sphere intersection), apply soft body deformation to the ShaderBall by displacing each vertex toward the helmet's center based on penetration depth, scaled inversely by the stiffness parameter. Store original vertex positions for recovery. (5) The deformation visually squishes the ShaderBall against the helmet surface, flattening the contact side. (6) After 1.5 seconds, animate vertex positions back to their original stored positions using a lerp driven by stiffness, simulating elastic recovery. (7) A 'Reset' button repositions the ShaderBall to its start location with restored geometry. (8) Validate all parameters on launch: clamp angle, velocity, and stiffness to their defined ranges and log warnings to an on-screen status div if values were clamped. Use requestAnimationFrame for the animation loop. Make the ShaderBall's material slightly translucent (opacity 0.85) to emphasize its jelly-like nature. Display a small HUD showing current deformation percentage during impact and recovery phases. Ensure both GLB models are loaded via GLTFLoader before enabling interaction.
